deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's 1953 notes on operator ideals in Hilbert spaces. 'Opérateur de Fredholm' here means trace-class (nuclear) operator, not the modern index-theoretic Fredholm operator. The previous page showed that Hilbert–Schmidt operators form a two-sided ideal with ||Au||_2 ≤ ||A|| ||u||_2. It identified $\overline{L^2(E,F)}\cong L^2(F,E)$ via $u\mapsto u^*$. It also showed $\|u\|_2=\|h\|_2$ for $h=\sqrt{u^*u}$, using the polar decomposition $u=Uh$, $h=Vu$ with U, V partial isometries.

Top of this page: in a suitable orthonormal basis the positive operator h is diagonal, with diagonal entries its eigenvalues $\rho_i$. Hence h is Hilbert–Schmidt iff $(\rho_i)\in\ell^2$, and then $\|h\|_2=(\sum\rho_i^2)^{1/2}$. This is the singular-value description of the Schatten 2-class.

Prop. 3: for Hilbert spaces E, F, the canonical map $\overline{E}\hat\otimes F\to L(E,F)$ is injective. Its image is the space of 'Fredholm' (trace-class) operators, with norm $\|\cdot\|_1$ the quotient projective norm.

Characterization: u is trace-class iff $h=\sqrt{u^*u}$ is, and then (20) $\|u\|_1=\|h\|_1=\sum\rho_i$. One may replace h by $\sqrt{uu^*}$.

Proof on this page:
- (i) Since $u=Uh$ and $h=Vu$ with $\|U\|,\|V\|\le1$, and the trace class is an operator ideal with $\|AuB\|_1\le\|A\|\|u\|_1\|B\|$, u and h are trace-class together and $\|u\|_1=\|h\|_1$.
- (ii) If h is trace-class it is compact, so $h=\sum\rho_i\,\bar a_i\otimes a_i$ with $(a_i)$ orthonormal. Let $p_n$ be the orthogonal projection onto span$(a_1,\dots,a_n)$. Then $\sum_1^n\rho_i=\mathrm{Tr}(p_nh)\le\|p_nh\|_1\le\|h\|_1$, so $\sum\rho_i\le\|h\|_1$.
- (iii) The converse is on the next page: $\|h\|_1\le\sum\rho_i\|a_i\|^2=\sum\rho_i$.

The following page derives the canonical form $u=\sum\rho_i\bar a_i\otimes b_i$ (Schmidt decomposition/SVD). It also gives $\|u\|_1=\mathrm{Tr}\sqrt{u^*u}$, the duality $\|u\|_1=\sup_{\|A\|\le1}|\mathrm{Tr}(Au)|$, and $\|vu\|_1\le\|v\|_2\|u\|_2$. Purpose: to identify, for Hilbert spaces, the projective tensor product with the Schatten–von Neumann trace class and the Hilbert tensor product with the Hilbert–Schmidt class, as a model case for nuclear operators.
errors: The diagonalization of h at the top of the page presupposes that h is compact (or that the H.-S. property is already assumed); a general positive operator need not have a pure point spectrum. Only the H.-S. direction is meant, so this is a presentational gap, not an error.
Step (i) relies on the ideal property of the projective (trace) norm, $\|AuB\|_1\le\|A\|\|u\|_1\|B\|$, which is used but not restated here. It is standard.
Step (ii) uses $|\mathrm{Tr}\,w|\le\|w\|_1$, i.e., that the trace is a norm-one functional on $\overline{E}\hat\otimes E$. This is well defined thanks to the injectivity in Prop. 3. Correct.

ideas.what: Injectivity of $\overline{E}\hat\otimes F\to L(E,F)$ for Hilbert spaces
ideas.modern_name: Hilbert spaces have the approximation property; projective tensor product = trace class
ideas.usually_credited_to: Schatten–von Neumann (1946–48); Grothendieck (1953–55) in general form
ideas.where_published: Produits tensoriels topologiques et espaces nucléaires (Mem. AMS 16, 1955); Résumé de la théorie métrique (1953/56)

ideas.what: Characterization of H.-S. and trace-class operators by the singular values of $|u|=\sqrt{u^*u}$, with $\|u\|_1=\sum\rho_i$
ideas.modern_name: Schatten classes S_2, S_1; singular values / s-numbers
ideas.usually_credited_to: E. Schmidt (1907), Schatten & von Neumann (1946–48), Schatten 'A theory of cross-spaces' (1950)
ideas.where_published: Produits tensoriels topologiques (1955), chapter on Hilbert spaces

ideas.what: Use of the polar decomposition u = Uh, h = Vu with contractions to transfer ideal norms between u and |u|
ideas.modern_name: Polar decomposition / ideal property of operator ideals

ideas.what: Lower bound $\sum\rho_i\le\|h\|_1$ via finite-rank projections and trace

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard working-out of the Schatten–von Neumann theory of trace-class and Hilbert–Schmidt operators in Grothendieck's tensor-product language. All of it was known by 1950 and appears in his 1955 Memoir. The only notable point is the historical terminology, 'opérateur de Fredholm' for trace class.
transcription_corrections: The formula label read as '(26)' is almost certainly '(20)': the next page refers back to it as '(20)' and continues the numbering with (21), (22).
Top line: likely 'Si l'on prend une base orthonormale convenable dans E' (or similar), so that h becomes diagonal; the sentence concerns the diagonalization of h.
In the struck-out text after Prop. 3, the eigenvalues are written as λ_i and then replaced by ρ_i in the final text.
The final line ends with 'Réciproquement, ...', continued on the next page with 'si h est compact et ... la série des valeurs propres ... sommable'.
The rotated left marginal note seems to be a cross-reference ('... Exp. ..., N° 1') rather than mathematical content; it is illegible beyond that.
